data.claim: Setting CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h (or settings subagentPromptCacheTtl; Claude Code 2.1.242+) raises the subagent prompt-cache TTL from 5m to 1h on this host, and a doctor check can report the effective TTL and warn while subagents still run on 5m.
data.falsifier: After setting the 1h TTL, new subagent transcripts still show only ephemeral_5m cache-creation tokens (no ephemeral_1h) — the aggregate script of TE-measure/TE-verify reads usage.cache_creation.
data.mechanism: Precedence per docs (agent-token-features.md 2.1, token-spend.md 5): FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1 overrides everything (forces 5m); then the subagent-specific knob CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL / subagentPromptCacheTtl; then ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1 raises both main and subagent to 1h; otherwise the subagent default stays 5m even on a subscription. A 1h write costs 2x vs 1.25x, netting ~-40-50% of subagent spend whenever gaps exceed 5m.
data.probe_output: 2.1.318 (Claude Code) — >= 2.1.242, so the 1h knob exists on this host
data.question: What is the effective subagent prompt-cache TTL on this host given the documented knobs, and does the installed Claude Code support the 1h setting?

Implemented ddflow/services/cachettl.py (effective_subagent_ttl precedence + doctor_notes + version gate), wired into ddflow/api/reporting/health.py doctor() as a note, added tests/test_cache_ttl_check.py matrix, and taught the Claude Code driver delta to launch subagents with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h. chunk_findings.detail: `doctor_notes` treats `verdict.ttl == "1h"` as a pass and never consults `one_hour_available`, and `effective_subagent_ttl` likewise stores `version` but does not fold it into `ttl`. Claude Code before 2.1.242 does not honor the subagent 1h knobs, so a host with `claude --version` `2.1.241` and `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` (or `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1`) still runs subagents on 5m, yet the note is `subagent cache TTL: 1h (via CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL)`. The same path passes when `claude --version` is missing or unparseable (`one_hour_available is None`), which the property docstring says must not be a pass. `_five_minute_remedy` only mentions the version when the computed TTL is already 5m, and the `forced` branch returns first, so `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` on 2.1.100 advises `set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` with no unavailable/upgrade note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cachettl.py:194

chunk_findings.detail: `test_doctor_note_quiet_on_one_hour` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` but, unlike `test_doctor_note_warns_on_five_minutes`, never clears `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` (and never stubs `read_settings`). Precedence in the same file puts `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` above the subagent env, so a process that already has `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` (or `true`) makes `doctor_notes` report a 5m forced TTL. The assertion `note.startswith("subagent cache TTL: 1h")` then fails even though the code under test followed the documented matrix.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_cache_ttl_check.py:test_doctor_note_quiet_on_one_hour

chunk_findings.detail: `test_doctor_note_quiet_on_one_hour` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` via `monkeypatch.setenv`, but does not stub `read_settings` to return empty settings in a way that overrides any pre-existing environment or settings state, nor does it clear `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` robustly across all test runs if environment leakage occurs. Furthermore, when `doctor_notes` runs in an environment where `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` is set or where settings conflict, the test assertion `assert note.startswith("subagent cache TTL: 1h")` fails because the effective TTL collapses to `5m`. This reproduces when `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M` is present in the test runner's execution environment.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_cache_ttl_check.py:149

chunk_findings.detail: `_five_minute_remedy` returns on `v.forced` before `one_hour_available`. Given `claude --version` `2.1.241` and `FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M=1` (with or without a 1h knob), `effective_subagent_ttl` stores that version but the note is `forced by FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M: unset it, then set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h`. Unsetting the force and setting 1h does not raise the TTL: this Claude Code ignores the knob, so the remedy tells the operator to do something that still leaves subagents on 5m.

chunk_findings.detail: A blank `subagentPromptCacheTtl` is treated as an explicit 5m choice and beats `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H`. The env path uses `(env.get(SUBAGENT_TTL_ENV) or "").strip()` and only wins when that string is non-empty, so `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=` falls through to the enable flag. The settings path uses `if subagent_setting is not None`, so `{"subagentPromptCacheTtl": ""}` or `"   "` is not absent: `str(...).strip().lower().startswith("1h")` is false, TTL becomes `"5m"` with source `"subagent_setting"`, and `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=1` is never read. Doctor then tells the operator to set a knob that is already present as blank, and subagents stay on 5 minutes.

chunk_findings.detail: `read_settings` builds `Path.home() / ".claude" / "settings.json"` before the `try`, so a missing home aborts the doctor instead of treating settings as unreadable. With `HOME` unset, `Path.home()` raises `RuntimeError` and `doctor_notes` never returns a note, despite the comment that probing must not fail the report.

chunk_findings.detail: `effective_subagent_ttl` only treats process env plus a top-level `subagentPromptCacheTtl` as inputs, and `read_settings` only merges `[REDACTED:path]` then `<repo>/.claude/settings.json`. Claude Code also applies `.claude/settings.local.json` on top of project settings, and injects a settings `env` object into the process it launches. Given settings.json `{"env": {"CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL": "1h"}}` (or the same key only in `.claude/settings.local.json`), with that var absent from the doctor process env and Claude Code 2.1.242+, this returns `SubagentTTL("5m", "default")` and `doctor_notes` warns to set the knob — while Claude already runs subagents at 1h. The reverse also fails: project `settings.json` has `subagentPromptCacheTtl: "1h"` and `settings.local.json` has `"5m"`; the doctor reports 1h and does not warn, so the 5-minute case this check exists to catch is silent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cachettl.py:176

chunk_findings.detail: The `read_settings` function calls `Path.home()` without catching `KeyError` or `PermissionError`, which can be raised on certain minimal or restricted environments (such as restricted container sandboxes where `$HOME` is unset or points to a non-existent directory), leading to an unhandled exception during `doctor_notes` execution.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cachettl.py:72

chunk_findings.detail: `read_settings` shallow-`update`s each settings file, so a later file's `env` object replaces the earlier one instead of merging keys. Given `[REDACTED:path]` `{"env": {"CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL": "1h"}}` and `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` or `settings.local.json` `{"env": {"ANTHROPIC_MODEL": "x"}}`, with that var absent from the process environment, `effective_subagent_ttl` returns `5m`/`default`. Claude Code keeps the user `env` entry under the project `env` object, so subagents actually run at 1h and doctor warns (or the reverse: a 1h only in the project `env` is dropped by a local `env` that does not repeat it, and doctor reports 1h).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cachettl.py:88

chunk_findings.detail: `_is_on` treats `yes` and `on` as enabled, but the docstring says the docs only accept `1` or `true`. Given `ENABLE_PROMPT_CACHING_1H=yes` (or `on`) and no subagent TTL knob, `effective_subagent_ttl` returns `1h`/`enable_1h` and `doctor_notes` does not warn. If the harness ignores those strings, subagents stay on 5m while doctor reports a 1h TTL.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cachettl.py:48

chunk_findings.detail: A subagent TTL is taken as 1h whenever the stripped value `startswith("1h")`, not only when it is `1h`. Given `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1hour` (or `1hx`), the function returns `1h`/`subagent_env`. A harness that only accepts the documented `1h`/`5m` tokens leaves the cache at 5m, so the doctor check passes on a value that does not raise the TTL.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/cachettl.py:172
